answer: Sybil resistance requires each identity to finish a domain-separated chain of modular squarings, with every square depending on the previous result; jade, juniper, and shale can serve as distinct input tags. GPUs may run separate chains concurrently, but cannot collapse one chain’s dependency depth, so creating clones multiplies the work and each identity remains bound by sequential hardware latency. A verifier can check the resulting Wesolowski proof efficiently without repeating the delay.
